samples.question: The upper panel shows a row of twelve upright gray bars of unequal height, with a colored square directly under each bar. The lower panel shows the same twelve items as gray spokes sticking out of a ring around a small gray hub, and a black dot sits just beyond the tip of exactly one spoke. The row is the ring cut open at one spoke and laid out flat: reading the ring clockwise starting from that spoke and continuing all the way around gives the bars from left to right. Which spoke the cut starts at is not shown and is not marked. The ring is never read counterclockwise and the pattern is never mirrored. The ring may be drawn at a different overall size than the row, and every spoke is scaled by that same single factor, so only the pattern of relative lengths is shared between the panels, never the absolute lengths, the angles or the positions. Each of the four square colors is used exactly three times, so no color by itself picks out a bar. Work out which bar in the row is the same item as the spoke carrying the black dot. What is the color of the square under that bar? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.
